## Context

The six write surfaces a leaf's own walk spawns. This is the subset of basicly-wpc8 that step 4 of the cutover waits on, and nothing more: the parent's remit is all 29 remaining spawn sites, and holding this behind the whole parent would hold the flip behind work the flip does not need.

Measured 2026-08-17 in the basicly-vkh0-29 worktree, by driving one intake-to-merge-to-ship walk over a temp consumer repo carrying the kit, a ledger seeded through the kit CLI, tracker mode owned, the manual runner and one required verify gate. With the binary genuinely off PATH the first advance raises RuntimeError: br is not on PATH from classify.py:73. Stubbing the spawn below br._mirror_write so the walk continues, six distinct surfaces spawn at nine events, every one a write except lint:

    update <id> -t <type>              1 spawn   classify.py:73
    lint <id> --json                   2 spawns  policy.py:200, fires on every advance
    sync --flush-only                  3 spawns  merge.py:520
    update <id> --external-ref <ref>   1 spawn   loop.py:2497
    sync --merge                       1 spawn   merge.py:466
    gate report --gate verify          1 spawn   verify.py:424
    close <id> --reason                1 spawn   loop.py:643

## The reason this is not a config edit

Under owned mode every engine read is already behind a flipped seam, and every engine write still goes to the binary and reaches the owned ledger only through br._mirror_write. Remove the binary and the write lands in neither store. basicly.toml's own comment says it: the rung above the dual write is not a config edit.

## What each surface needs

- update -t and update --external-ref are field writes, and the field kind already exists in the log.
- close --reason is already one of the mirror's six surfaces.
- gate report is mirrored on the write side; its read side is the gate listing, which is one of the five operations with no owned equivalent.
- lint --json is the definition-of-ready lint, the first of those five operations, and it is a design question rather than a port: porting it means owning the validation rules.
- sync --flush-only and sync --merge do not get ported. They reconcile the binary's database with its JSONL export, and with one store there is nothing to reconcile, so they are deleted rather than replaced.

## Out of scope, deliberately

The parent's other classes: dep add, dep cycles, create, blocked, show, init, and the sites in decompose, supervise, loop_state, worktree, cli, validate_gate, rubrics and tracker_cutover. Those are the parent's remainder and none of them fires on a leaf's intake-to-merge path.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/classify.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_classify.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Found by `basicly-8g719r` and proved with a positive control rather than inferred.

`dropin.compose` keys `rebaselined` by **entry**, so N fragments each declaring a delta on the same file
are reported as **one** rebaseline. Measured: `tests/test_loop.py` carries four declarations, 311 plus
146 plus 13 plus 109, reported as one; `merge.py` carries three, 79 plus 192 plus 208.

`basicly.d/README.md` states the count exists *so a rebaseline cannot accumulate the way a frozen delta
silently did*. **It can.** The entries do bind individually - a deliberately short delta fails the gate,
which is the positive control - so nothing is wrongly admitted; what is wrong is the count an operator
reads to judge how much debt a file has taken, and the README's claim about it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Find a file with more than one basicly.d fragment declaring a module size delta on it.
2. Run the module size gate and read the rebaselined count in its summary line.
3. Observe the count treats the several declarations as one.
4. Shorten one declaration deliberately and observe the gate fail, which is the positive control that each entry binds.
5. Read the claim in basicly.d/README.md about the count preventing accumulation and observe it does not hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given several fragments declaring a delta on one file then the reported rebaseline count names each declaration - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_dropin.py -k accumulated -q`
- Given the README claim then it states what the count actually prevents

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dropin.py`
- `basicly.d/README.md`
- `tests/test_dropin.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/dropin.py`
- `basicly.d/README.md`
- `tests/test_dropin.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`
payload.title: the rebaseline count under reports because it keys by entry so several fragments naming one file count once

payload.text:
A measured instance, 2026-08-20, for the claim this record makes about accumulation.

tests/test_handoff.py carries three separate rebaseline fragments: basicly-pp7q4i 3986 to 4134, basicly-gvlpxm 4134 to 5124, basicly-u2hl.59 5124 to 6302. Plus 58 percent on one file, and the count keys by entry so those three read as one - which is exactly what this record says basicly.d/README.md claims is prevented.

Two details that sharpen the finding beyond the count. All three fragments gave the same reason and deferred the same extraction, the cut_violation move into artifact_record; that extraction has since landed, so the reason is now stale and nothing re-examined it. And all three named tests/test_handoff_schemas.py as the home with the room while calling it out of scope - it has 2158 tokens free and is the wrong responsibility, validating schema files with no repo fixture and no handoff.record call. A deferral justified on room outlives the room.

So the accumulation is not only invisible to the count, it is invisible to the reason: each fragment restates a predecessor's justification without testing whether it still holds. A useful discriminator would be to refuse a rebaseline naming a file that already has one, unless the fragment states what changed since the last.

Resolved for this file rather than conceded: the corrupted-artifact section moved to test_handoff_states.py under basicly-kmqno2, and test_handoff.py fell to 5784 - the first fall across those three concessions.

Closed by baae6d59. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4501 tests.

The number this record predicted, measured on the tree: 41 declarations were reported as 19. The gate's summary line now reads '41 rebaselined across 19 entries'. tests/test_loop.py carried four - 311, 146, 13, 109 - reported as one; merge.py three.

So 22 of 41 loosenings were invisible. Every entry always bound individually, which this record already proved with a positive control, so nothing was wrongly admitted; what was wrong is that the number an operator reads to judge a file's debt was the count of FILES, and the whole point of counting is to watch debt accumulate on a file. Per-entry counting was exactly blind to the property the README claimed it guaranteed.

Baseline.rebaselined maps an entry to EVERY declaring fragment rather than the last. That is the only interface change. The composed baseline is asserted unchanged, which is the control that accumulating the names did not move the arithmetic. Mutation restoring last-declarer-wins fails both new tests.

The README now states what the count really prevents - each loosening visible, one file taking several not stopped - carries the 41-against-19 measurement, and says a file appearing in several fragments is the signal to split it.

THIS FINDING EXPLAINS THREE EARLIER ONES IN THE SAME PASS. tests/test_handoff.py had been rebaselined three times and merge.py three, and I found both by reading basicly.d/ by hand while the gate reported one apiece. The instrument that would have shown me the accumulation was the one being fixed. Recorded on basicly-8ro0nx and basicly-e2r08j as the reason those measurements had to be taken by hand.

Not done: nothing refuses a second rebaseline on a file that already has one. The count now shows the accumulation; it does not stop it. A gate that required a fragment to state what changed since the last rebaseline on the same entry is the control, and it is not filed.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When the terminal and handily sessions use basicly, I want the traps they reported fixed in one patch release, so they can drop their local workarounds and stop paying a retry or a hidden wrong state for each.

## Scope

Fixes only: bugs and guidance lines reported by consumer sessions on 2026-10-13. No feature work; the repository-name and port features stay out.

## Order

1. Wrong state with no warning (priority 1): basicly-xy5b2j4, basicly-s4ia3qh, basicly-q2tb4qj, basicly-5bv6uxj.
2. Wrong advice in the default shell (priority 1): basicly-g81t6eb.
3. Refusals that name no fix (priority 2): basicly-fyyb3xa, basicly-bvc1vky, basicly-nni87i5, basicly-vtwagru.
4. Measurement gap (priority 2, may slip to the next release): basicly-lnrd6vx.
5. Guidance lines, one batch (priority 3): basicly-lr1xjgp, basicly-07b1eo6, basicly-qf98ra9, basicly-nt1xl6h. basicly-u5l0ymi closes as superseded when basicly-xy5b2j4 lands.

## Done

Every child closed or moved out with a reason, each fix with a regression test and a release note, and both sessions told which of their local lines they can drop.

Owner 2026-10-13: "prioritize the reported consumer issues and create a plan for next release that is focused on fixes only".

## Trigger

When a Claude Code mod reads the tracker, I want a slim normalized item list, so I can read every item inside the 4 MiB stdout limit of a mod process.

## Context

handily CLI adapter contract v1, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-07 (handily plan revision 3). `cmd items --json` prints a JSON array of items with id, title, status (open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, closed or other), rawStatus, priority, type, assignee, updatedAt and source. `cmd describe --json` prints name, version, contract 1, watch globs, write argv prefixes and statusMap. Measured by handily: `basicly tracker list` prints 8,484,867 bytes in this repo, and a mod's process.run keeps at most 4 MiB, so the JSON is cut off.

- Standard library only.
- Keep the existing list and show output unchanged.

When the tracker documentation demonstrates loss acknowledgment, I want the consumer test to supply an actual known sequence gap, so I can prove successful recovery and preserve healthy-ledger refusal.

## Steps to Reproduce

Full verification fails the documented REFERENCE.md acknowledge-loss command because the generic consumer fixture has no missing sequence9. The command correctly refuses currentmissing[] versus requested[9]. Existing recovery API and copied-kit positive-gap tests pass. This is a missing operation precondition in the documentation consumer test, not a reason to accept acknowledgments on healthy history.

- `tests/test_kit_tracker_docs.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/REFERENCE.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

Leave REFUSED_ON_A_FRESH_LEDGER unchanged. For the documented acknowledge-loss command only, seed real CLI comment events until requested sequence9 has a later survivor, then remove exactly that matched record/sequence fixture line in the scratch ledger. Run the unchanged documented argv and assert the resulting explicit acknowledgment while the original sequence remains absent. Add a separate healthy-ledger invocation with nonzero exit, exact missing-set refusal and byte-identical entire ledger. Explain the required gap and healthy refusal in the reference if useful. No production parser or recovery rule change is authorized.

## Confirmation Plan

Run the complete documented-command and loss-acknowledgment suites and execute the documented command through a fresh standalone package installation.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while probing the swallow on a scratch ledger. Two sites report a tracker write as having happened when it did not, and they are the sites `basicly-kn4rip` left because its own change was additive.

## The kit CLI crashes rather than reports

`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py:322` reads `appended[0].record` with no guard. When every draft is swallowed - the ordinary outcome of re-recording a fact the ledger holds - `appended` is `[]` and the CLI raises an unhandled `IndexError` with a traceback. That is the kit-side twin of the engine-seam defect `79bbe0db` just fixed, and that commit does not cover it: the kit is a separate consumer with its own entry point, which is the whole reason it takes a ledger directory as an argument.

A traceback is a worse answer than the wrong one it replaces. An operator reads it as a broken tool rather than as a write that recorded nothing.

## Two engine sites still report a swallowed gate as recorded

`basicly-kn4rip` made `tracker.write` return whether every draft landed. Its own commit message says every other caller discards that return and that the change is therefore additive. That is true, and two of those callers are where it costs something:

- `src/basicly/verify.py:415`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py:536`

Both discard the boolean and unconditionally print `recorded gate <name>=<status>`.

**`gate report` is the verb with the worst swallow shape.** Its payload is `{provenance, gate, provider, passed}` (`src/basicly/write_verbs.py:227-235`) and carries neither the note nor the actor, so two genuine runs of the same gate with the same verdict are byte-identical and the second is skipped. This is a plain A then A - it needs no intervening B, unlike every other verb. `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/gates.py:222-224` documents the shape as wrong.

So a gate that really ran twice is recorded once, and both call sites say it was recorded.

## Steps to Reproduce

**The kit crash.** On a throwaway ledger under a scratch directory - never `.basicly/ledger/`:

1. `uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create <dir> --prefix scratch --title probe --status open`
2. `... update <dir> <id> --status blocked`
3. `... update <dir> <id> --status open`

**Observed.** Step 3 exits with `IndexError: list index out of range` at `cli.py:322`.
**Expected.** It reports that the fact was already held and nothing was appended.
**Control.** Steps 1 and 2 both succeed and print a record and an event id, so the CLI works and step 3's failure is the swallow path specifically.

**The gate report.** Record the same gate, provider and verdict twice on a scratch record and read the record's events: one `gate` event, two reports of success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every draft a kit CLI write hands the ledger is skipped, THE CLI SHALL report that and SHALL NOT raise.
- WHEN a gate report records nothing because the ledger already holds it, THE CALLER SHALL NOT print that it was recorded.
- WHEN two genuine runs of one gate produce the same verdict, THE LEDGER SHALL be able to hold both, or the caller SHALL say which one it kept.
- WHERE the engine reports a gate, THE REPORT SHALL rest on what the write returned rather than on no exception having been raised.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: `basicly-kn4rip`
- demonstration: Drive the kit CLI through a swallowed write and read a report instead of a traceback, then report one gate twice and read the second report against the record's actual event count.

payload.text:
[reproduced on landed main 2026-08-22] basicly-kn4rip has landed (95989616, 943622a1) and fixed the ENGINE SEAM half: tracker_write.py:46 now prints 'already recorded, so nothing was appended' and tracker.write returns a bool. The kit half is untouched and still crashes.

Reproduced against main at 61a5ac1c, on a throwaway ledger under the session scratchpad, never .basicly/ledger/:

  uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create <dir> --prefix scratch --title 'swallow probe' --status open
  ... update <dir> <id> --add-label demo        -> event appended
  ... update <dir> <id> --remove-label demo     -> event appended
  ... update <dir> <id> --add-label demo        -> IndexError: list index out of range

The site is unchanged at .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py:320, inside the write branch:

  appended = write(args, redact)
  return EXIT_OK, {'record': appended[0].record, ...}

When every draft is swallowed, appended is [] and the subscript raises. A traceback is a worse answer than the wrong one it replaces: an operator reads it as a broken tool rather than as a write that recorded nothing.

Control from the same run: steps one and two both succeed and print a record and an event id, so the CLI works and only the swallow path fails. A second control, from the engine side: the seam refused an unknown record with a clear sentence rather than a traceback, which is the shape this site should take.

Note the seam guards a different thing well - 'names a record the ledger does not hold ... accepting it would fold that id into existence' - so the kit is the only consumer left raising.

payload.description:
## The defect

23 record and kind pairs hold artifacts cut at 4096 bytes. Their entry predicate refuses them with a schema type violation on the top-level instance and a 300-character fragment of the cut JSON. The reason the reader sees names neither truncation nor the original length, so the block looks like a malformed artifact rather than a transport that destroyed a valid one.

`basicly-ejdm` is open and blocked this way. Its loop status reports a different, coexisting cause, so nothing on any surface names the real one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call the entry predicate for the implementation-plan of `basicly-ejdm` and read the reason.
2. Note the stored event carries a truncation flag and the original byte length beside it.
3. Run loop status on the same record.

Observed: the reason is a JSON fragment. The truncation flag sitting on the same event is never mentioned.
Expected: the reason names truncation, both byte counts, and re-recording as the remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a stored body carrying a truncation flag then the verdict's reason names truncation and the original byte length, and does not report a schema type violation on the top-level instance.
Given the body is unrecoverable then the verdict names re-recording as the remedy.
Given an artifact that is malformed but not truncated then the reason is unchanged.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly loop status basicly-ejdm reporting a reason naming truncation and both byte counts, plus uv run pytest tests/test_handoff.py -q

## Note

Independent of T3 and worth landing first: it changes a message, costs nothing, and makes the other 22 stop lying about why they were refused.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/handoff.py`
- `tests/test_handoff.py`

payload.text:
scope widened by one file, with the proof

The lane stopped without writing code and proved why: the truncation flag never reaches
`handoff.entry_verdict`. `comment_rows.from_ledger` projects each comment event's payload
down to two keys, text and the stamp, so `text_truncated` and `text_original_length_bytes`
are discarded one seam below the declared scope. Three projection sites confirm it, not one:
`comment_rows.from_ledger`, `tracker._rendered` and `tracker.export_comment_texts`.

Proven on a real write-and-read path in a temporary ledger, with the event side as the
positive control: the event payload carries all four keys, the row carries two. Reproduced
read-only against the committed ledger for basicly-ejdm, which holds text_truncated true and
text_original_length_bytes 5304.

The lane declined to add a read-the-flag-if-present branch inside its fence, because no
producer of rows carries those keys, so the branch would be unreachable in production and
testable only against a fabricated row shape. That is the right call under the dead-code rule.

Scope therefore adds `src/basicly/comment_rows.py` and its test file. The file is in no other
record's scope, so this is an unowned gap rather than another lane's ground.

Two constraints measured before any edit: handoff.py is frozen at 69.2 percent comment density
and may only fall, with 331 tokens of size headroom, so the diff must add more code than prose.

The demonstration line in this record is not reachable and is replaced: loop status cannot
print the artifact reason, because the verdict is consulted only at the decompose-to-build
fan-out and basicly-ejdm is blocked earlier on a missing verify gate. The substitute is a
direct entry_verdict call on basicly-ejdm, an unchanged admitted control, and a malformed
but untruncated artifact whose reason must stay unchanged.

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-e2mz.6` landed `.github/workflows/improvement-loop.yml` with `workflow_dispatch` only, by
owner decision 2026-08-14. That decision is explicit that it confirms `workflow_dispatch` and
**not** a cron trigger.

So one half of `e2mz.6` acceptance bullet 1 is deliberately unmet: "then `basicly loop improve`
runs **without a human invoking it**". `workflow_dispatch` cannot satisfy it by construction. The
other half - `wired-or-deleted` crediting the command from an independent entry rather than from
the script own docstring - is met and carries a control assertion.

## What this is

A `schedule:` trigger on the existing file. It would be this repository first scheduled workflow:
`.github/workflows/` holds `basicly.yml`, `improvement-loop.yml`, `pages.yml`, `quality-gates.yml`
and `release.yml`, and none carries `schedule:`.

## The precondition the owner named

"Watching it file a few more under a human hand before it runs unattended is cheap, and the
one-lane bound means an unattended loop that misbehaves would still only produce one bad bead at a
time - **but only if the bound holds, which is itself only observed once**."

The bound has now been observed holding twice, both against real tracker state. That is not the
few the decision asks for. Do not read this bead as ready on the count alone.

## The second question a schedule forces, which dispatch did not

The workflow dry-runs, because a live run files a bead into an ephemeral checkout and persisting
it needs `contents: write` and a push to `main` from CI. A scheduled dry run reports into a log
nobody reads, so a schedule is only worth having if the actuator can persist - which makes the
push the real design question behind this bead rather than the cron line.

CI files are on the confirmation list and this needs its own confirmation.
payload.title: give the improvement loop a schedule trigger so it runs without a human pressing a button

39.4% of this tree is prose rather than code, measured in the sizing governor's own token unit across src, tests, .scripts and .basicly/core. Recent commits add comments at 35.5% of added code lines against 10.5% mid-history.

Nothing binds: no fragment mentions comments, ERA001 only catches commented-out code, and python-guidelines currently forbids deleting a comment. A purge hook cannot be the instrument - it would strip the 64 pragma comments the lint gates read, and ruff D mandates docstrings so the prose would relocate.

Deliver:
1. .scripts/check_comment_density.py - a frozen-baseline ratchet on prose tokens (comments excluding pragmas, plus docstrings) as a share of module tokens, cap 50%, waiver marker counted, mirroring check_module_size.py.
2. [tool.comment_density] in pyproject.toml with the go-live baselines.
3. A [[verify.checks]] fast entry in basicly.toml.
4. A core-rules fragment line making code the authoritative source, and an amendment to python-guidelines so the do-not-delete rule does not license the density.

## Context

Parent: basicly-lc2bd3v. The owner: *"start, stop work"*.

`lane-kill` is already in `board_actions.ACTIONS` and already works. It has no surface: `board_asks.pending` draws a row per *ask*, and a running lane is not an ask, so the verb is unreachable unless something else happens to be waiting.

That is the whole defect. A verb that exists and cannot be pressed is worse than one that does not exist, because a reader of the code believes it is available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running, THE BOARD SHALL offer to kill it, on that lane`s own card.
- THE REASON SHALL be a required free-text field, so the ledger records why a lane was stopped rather than that it was.
- WHERE `lanes[]` is absent from the snapshot, THE BOARD SHALL offer nothing rather than an action naming an empty id.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_asks.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_asks.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: dispatch a pass, press kill on its card, and read the worktree gone

payload.description:
On a fresh consumer repo, basicly install cannot auto-activate the git hooks. When pre-commit is not on PATH, install_hooks falls back to `uv run pre-commit` (hooks.py), which only resolves if the consumer repo declares pre-commit as a project dependency — a fresh consumer never does — so uv reports "Failed to spawn: pre-commit (program not found)" and the gates are left inert with a confusing message. Separately, a target folder without a .git directory cannot have hooks activated at all (pre-commit install needs a git repo), and today that surfaces as an opaque error rather than clear guidance.

Verified locally: `uv run pre-commit --version` in a fresh dir fails to spawn pre-commit, while `uv tool run pre-commit --version` (uvx) auto-provisions it and works. The consumer reliably has uv (basicly is installed via uvx), so uvx is the correct runner.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a fresh folder that has no .git and no pyproject declaring pre-commit.
2. Ensure pre-commit is not on PATH (only uv is available).
3. Run basicly install in that folder.
4. Observe: "Could not auto-activate git hooks: pre-commit install failed (error: Failed to spawn: pre-commit ... program not found); run manually: pre-commit install ...". The manual command also fails because pre-commit is not installed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- install_hooks and uninstall_hooks fall back to `uv tool run pre-commit` (uvx) instead of `uv run pre-commit` when pre-commit is not on PATH, so a consumer with only uv gets pre-commit auto-provisioned and activation succeeds.
- The "run manually" guidance points at a command that actually works without pre-commit pre-installed (uvx pre-commit install --install-hooks ...).
- When the target repo has no .git directory, activation is skipped with a clear actionable message (not a git repository; run git init then basicly hooks-build), and basicly install still exits 0 with projections written.
- Regression tests cover: the uvx fallback command is chosen when pre-commit is absent but uv is present; the no-.git path returns the clear guidance without spawning pre-commit.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

Fix the runner fallback and the no-.git precheck in hooks.py plus the caller message in cli.py. No change to the happy path (pre-commit on PATH). No new dependency. Does not change what hooks are projected, only how activation is invoked and guarded.
payload.title: Install cannot auto-activate git hooks on a fresh consumer repo

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a ledger holds same-ID copies with different JSON value types, I want scrub to validate every stored copy before redaction, so I can refuse corrupt input without rewriting another file.

## Steps to Reproduce

In a scratch ledger, place a valid seq=1 created event first, a same-ID copy with seq=true or seq=1.0 in a shard, and a separate actor value needing redaction. The duplicate independently fails events.from_json. Current scrub returns one changed line and rewrites the trunk while the malformed shard remains unchanged. Payload extra values integer1 versus true or1.0 also collapse under Python dictionary equality and bypass the unique-only generation check. Four concrete probes reproduced this behavior; existing standalone compaction tests already refuse typed duplicate differences.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_scrub_ledger.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Repair Boundary

Keep the current all-input preflight and generation validation. Parse every nonempty stored event before deduplication. Reuse the existing kit event serialization for typed stored identity comparison, retaining raw field-presence comparison. Refuse all malformed or divergent copies before publishing any redaction. Preserve identical copies, valid generation holes, unchanged IDs and withdrawal audit remapping. Do not rewrite the live ledger or change any gate.

## Confirmation Plan

Run the focused scrub, generation, shard and withdrawal regression files and a packaged standalone-typed-identity plus engine consumer refusal proof.
payload.requirements: Keep the existing kit parser and typed event serialization authoritative. Preserve all copies and bytes on refusal, normal scrub behavior and integrity gates.

## Trigger

When a release note entry loses its list bullet and markdownlint passes anyway because an unbulleted paragraph is valid markdown, I want a check that catches a non-bullet entry inside a changelog list, so I can stop a reader seeing prose where every sibling is a bullet.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value: A check shall detect a changelog entry inside a version section's list (for example `### Added`) that is not a list item. The check shall run as part of the gate suite, not only as a one-time manual fix. The check shall not flag a legitimate non-list line such as a `Delta:` header.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- [ ] A check reads a changelog section's list and flags a paragraph at column 0 that is not a `- ` line or its continuation.
- [ ] The check does not flag a genuine non-list line such as a `Delta:` header.
- [ ] The check runs as part of the existing gate suite, not as a one-off fix.
- [ ] Re-running the check against the five previously bulletless v0.9.0 entries shows them passing.

payload.description:
## Context

Two claims about GitHub Copilot were stated to the owner as fact and both were wrong,
2026-08-06. Copilot was said to report no token counts: GitHub moved every plan to
token-based billing on 2026-06-01, the CLI exposes a per-model breakdown, and this
repo's own `runner.py` has been extracting it from copilot's session store all along.

The failure was not a missing tool - WebSearch was available throughout. It was
**trusting a summary line in our own docs about a third party**:
`docs/design/factory-design.md` carried 'copilot has no counts' in a components table
while section 7.5 four hundred lines below documented the exact extraction mechanism.

## What the skill encodes

An order of evidence that puts **our own code that already touches the interface**
first, vendor docs second, and marketing nowhere; the rule to read the section a
summary cites; version-and-date pinning, which this repo already does well where it
does it at all; the distinction between a capability existing and our dispatch being
able to reach it; stating a claim at the precision the evidence supports, so a
correct-but-vague note does not invite a future reader to 'fix' it; and correcting the
document that carried the stale version rather than adding the new claim beside it.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/interface-facts/skill.yaml`

> That is the same population `supervise.advance_parked` drives each pass, on purpose: what drains the bound is exactly what the bound counts, so a blocked pass is not a wedged one.

That claim is false. A unit whose derived phase is `validate` is counted by `wip.downstream_units` (wip.py:140-144), is never dispatched (`supervise.py:1577` takes `phase == "build"` only), and is never advanced. Five such units refuse every further dispatch. The queue item raised then (`WIP_QUESTION`, wip.py:50) tells the operator to land the finished lanes, which `advance_parked` cannot do for this population.

## Why it is one day old

VALIDATE became a real phase on 2026-08-13 under `basicly-u2hl.54`. That bead carried five acceptance criteria. All five concerned the phase, its gate, its refusal and its dispatch. None named the supervisor's parked-lane driver. The close was correct against the criteria and the work was incomplete against the system.

## The decision the implementer must take

`advance_parked` calls `loop.run_until_blocked`, which passes no `grant_root` and defaults `repair_dispatch=True` (loop.py:2444-2462). Adding `"validate"` to the tuple naively would run `_dispatch_validation` outside the spend gate. The acceptance criteria pin that.

## Acceptance

- While a supervised session holds a unit whose derived phase is `validate`, when a pass runs, then the engine advances that unit or enqueues a decision naming it, and never skips it silently.
- When the phase set that `advance_parked` drives is compared with the set that `wip` counts, then one definition exists and the other imports it.
- If a validation dispatch is reachable from a supervised pass, then it checks `policy.spend_status` under the session grant root before it spawns.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/wip.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_wip.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py tests/test_wip.py -q` with a new test that parks an L3 unit in validate and asserts a supervised pass routes it.

## Warning

`supervise.py` and `wip.py` are both density-frozen at zero headroom. Move the tuple. Do not add prose.

payload.description:
## The defect

A dispatched validator can execute successfully, be charged for, and leave the loop in **exactly** the state it was in. No gate event, no queued decision, no rework charged. The advance exits and the operator cannot tell the run happened from any loop surface.

So a lane at `validate` cannot leave `validate` by advancing, and the only signal that anything ran is the spend.

## Measured on basicly-gvlpxm, 2026-08-20

`basicly loop advance basicly-gvlpxm` merged the repair (main advanced to `7381a145`) and then dispatched, per the `[harness-run]` records on the record, all with `outcome: executed` and `returncode: 0`:

- one `claude --agent validator`
- two `claude --agent reviewer`, lenses `correctness` and `security`

One of those runs alone records `cost: 1.1256025` and `tokens: 506272`.

**The ledger holds two gate events for this record and both predate today:**

```
2026-08-19T20:18:36 | {"gate": "verify", "passed": true}
2026-08-19T20:27:10 | {"gate": "validate-as-consumer", "passed": false}
```

Event kinds for the record: `created 5, status 1, edge 2, field 2, comment 20, artifact 1, gate 2`. After the advance, `loop status` still reports `failed: validate-as-consumer` and `rework: validate-as-consumer=1`, both unchanged, and `basicly loop decisions basicly-gvlpxm --json` returns `[]`.

Positive control, required because this is a claim about an absence: gate events ARE written by this engine and have the right shape - the two above are them. So the mechanism works and today's validator run did not reach it.

## Why the wrong probe is the trap here

Gate results are **ledger events**, not comments, and `basicly tracker show` does not surface them. I first probed the record's comments, found no validator verdict among 16, and nearly filed a different bug. The reviewers DO leave `[harness-review]` comments, which makes the absence of a validator comment look like the defect. It is not. **Probe `.basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` for `kind: gate`; a comment scan cannot see a gate either way.**

## Why this matters more than one stuck lane

The lane is wedged in a way that costs money to discover and burns the rework budget to escape. Because the gate stays `failed`, the next advance re-enters `_on_validate`'s `required_failed` branch. The branch now has no commit base does not hold, so `_repair_from_validate` takes `_worktree_landed` to `_repair_in_place`, whose brief was consumed on read - so it returns None, `_repair_from_validate` returns None, and `_on_validate` falls through to `_rework`. That charges the second and last rework slot for a round in which nothing was wrong with the code.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a record at phase `validate` whose `validate-as-consumer` gate is recorded failed and whose worktree branch carries a repair commit base does not hold.
2. Run `basicly loop advance <id>`.
3. Observe the merge succeed and base advance.
4. Observe `[harness-run]` records appear on the record for a validator and one reviewer per lens, each `outcome: executed`.
5. Run `grep -h '<id>' .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` and count events of `kind: gate`.
6. Observe the count is unchanged from before step 2, and `loop status` reports the same gate verdict and the same rework count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a validator that executes at validate when the advance completes then a gate event is recorded for validate-as-consumer carrying its verdict - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop_validate.py -k records_a_gate -q`
- Given a validator that executes and returns no usable verdict when the advance completes then the advance blocks with a queued decision naming the validator rather than exiting with no state change - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop_validate.py -k no_verdict_blocks -q`
- Given an advance in which no validator was dispatched then no gate event is recorded so the fix does not manufacture a verdict - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop_validate.py -k undispatched -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/validate_gate.py`
- `tests/test_loop_validate.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/validate_gate.py`
- `tests/test_loop_validate.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_loop_validate.py -q`

## Context

Measured 2026-09-01 on a clone of this repo at commit 7e858322, folded in the clone own uv environment so the reading is not an artifact of a borrowed interpreter.

```text
working checkout:  board: sections  11 rendered, 0 withheld, 1 not emitted
fresh clone:       board: sections   7 rendered, 0 withheld, 5 not emitted
```

The five the clone loses are `gates`, `health`, `lanes`, `session` and `spend`. Four of them are absent for one reason: their producers read `.basicly/usage/`, which the repo git-ignores, and a clone has no such directory at all. `board_usage.gates` reads it; `run_record.load_run_records` reads `.basicly/usage/run-records.json` and feeds both `health` and `spend`; `session_facts` needs a supervisor lock that has never been taken. The `Act` panel disappears with them. `lanes` is a separate defect with its own record.

The ready set travels fine - the clone drew 211 ready rows - so this is not a ledger problem. It is that half the board is derived from a store that never leaves the machine that wrote it. An operator on a new clone reads a board that says a producer did not measure, and concludes the tool is broken.

basicly-0eexh5 and basicly-7hebuh made *grant* spend travel by writing a typed `dispatch` event into the committed ledger. The board `spend` panel does not read that path, so the same figure is on the board and off it depending on the checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the board is folded on a checkout that holds committed ledger dispatch events and no `.basicly/usage/` directory, THE `spend` SECTION SHALL be emitted from the committed ledger.
- WHEN no run history exists in either store, THE SECTION SHALL still be omitted rather than emitted as a zero.
- WHEN the board is folded on a checkout with no gate history, THE `gates` SECTION SHALL name that the history is local rather than reading as an unmeasured producer.
- WHEN `basicly board` runs on a fresh clone, ITS section line SHALL report fewer than five sections not emitted.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_usage.py`
- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_board_usage.py`
- `tests/test_board_snapshot.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `basicly board --out` on a fresh clone reports a smaller not-emitted count and draws a spend panel

The proposed repair, a ledger-derived spend section, cannot be made honest today: the committed ledger holds 4 dispatch events against 398 machine-local records, and each carries only tokens and spend_micros - no cost and no input, output or cache split - so a section built from it would render as the repository's lifetime spend while being about 2 percent of it, with every other cell empty. ## Retro proposal, not applied

Session 2026-09-12. Awaiting the owner decision; a retro finding is never self-applied.

## The incident, twice in one session
Asked whether the bandit gate covers `packages/`, I ran `bandit -q -c pyproject.toml -r src .scripts packages` and reported a failure. The declared check is `bandit -q -c pyproject.toml -r .scripts .basicly/core/hooks .basicly/core/kit`. My invented path list produced a finding the real gate does not have, and I retracted it.

The same shape had already happened with the kits: `uv run --project packages/basicly-tier` reported all three kits broken, because that path reads the source tree where `force-include` has not run. Also retracted.

## Root cause, and why it is not a discipline failure
There is no way to run one declared check. `basicly verify` takes `--mode`, not a check name, so the only route to "run just this gate" is to retype its argv from `basicly.toml` - or, as happened, to approximate it.

Measured on `.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json`: `bandit` 19 direct invocations, `vulture` 67, `pyright` 267, `lint-imports` 140. `verify` appears once. The tools are run directly essentially always, and every direct run is an argv nobody checked against the declared one.

The `core-rules` fragment already says the authority is the code that reads it, not the docs. The authority here is `basicly.toml`, and the harness offers no way to obey it.

## Proposal
`basicly verify --only <name>` runs exactly one `[[verify.checks]]` entry with its declared argv, and refuses an unknown name by listing the ones that exist.

## Why this rather than a hook
A guard on hand-rolled invocations would fire on 493 recorded calls, most of them legitimate narrowing. The cheaper fix is to make the correct path exist, so the improvisation has a named alternative.

## Scope
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
**The title is refuted as written.** "Instead of spawning a headless CLI" cannot be delivered:
the Python Agent SDK (`claude-agent-sdk`) drives the installed CLI as a local subprocess -
`CLINotFoundError` and its own transport documentation say so. What changes is **how a
definition is loaded**, not whether a subprocess exists. Restate as: *spawn the role definition
as a subagent so its declared `skills:` preload and per-subagent usage is emitted.*

**A third of the text below argues a settled point.** The section "The decision this
contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident" attacks `agent-roster-design.md:210`
and `factory-loop-requirements.md:602`. **Neither file exists** - all six design notes were
absorbed and deleted in `28257e9` on 2026-08-08, one day before this bead's last edit. And the
position was reversed *in this bead's favour* on 2026-08-09: **D27** (`factory-loop.md:105`)
decides "thin engine: the catalog defines, the host executes... the host runtime spawns the
subagent, resolves its tier and fires the boundary hooks", and **D28** amends the Conductor
refusal because "both installed runtimes contradict it by construction".

**Its gating open question is now answered, and the answer changes the scope.** An externally
spawned process is always a separate session and can **never** appear as a subagent row inside
a live interactive session. Non-interactive host dispatch: yes. Nested in the driving session:
never. So the bead's own re-scope branch - the engine emits work a session executes - is a
genuinely different design that must be chosen deliberately rather than fallen into.

**The plan's justification for this row does not survive checking.**
`implementation-plan.md:225` says the question is "answered twice over", citing a competing
harness that "runs exactly this split in production". `factory-loop.md:1115` says that
harness's loop does **not** call any LLM and emits a prompt to stdout - which is an existence
proof for the re-scope branch, not for engine-driven host dispatch.

**The real content is the spawn mode**, and it is measured: `skills:` is honoured for a spawned
subagent and **not** under `claude --agent <name> -p`, this repo's only dispatch shape. That is
`basicly-ey58`, which this bead should depend on. One sub-claim below is also stale: `.claude/`
agents are no longer inert - `roles.py:93-105` stats them and `runner.py:547-570` injects
`--agent` - but **0 of 346 recorded dispatches carry it**, against a positive control of 163
carrying `-p`, so the effect is still nil.

The four non-negotiables below - D1's singleton supervisor, D9's `prompt_sha256`, metering, and
agnosticism as contract - are all still current and survive the restatement.

---

## Context

Every dispatch in this engine ends at one `subprocess.Popen` (`runner.py:1469`) of a CLI
binary — `("claude","-p",PROMPT)`, `("codex","exec",PROMPT)`, `("copilot","-p",PROMPT)`
(`runner.py:275-308`). **No code path anywhere asks the host to run a subagent.**

Measured 2026-08-08: flags actually passed are `--output-format`, `--verbose`,
`--forward-subagent-text`, `--session-id`, `--disallowedTools`, `--model`. **Zero hits**
for `--agents`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--mcp-config`, `--permission-mode`, `--resume`.

And the agents we do project are inert: `.claude/agents/` holds three files written by
`agents.sync()`, and **no dispatch code reads that directory** — its only other consumer
is `cli.py:1261`, which globs it to *delete* files.

## The decision this contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident

`agent-roster-design.md:210` refuses this by name:

> role prompts *"cannot be Claude subagent files — the factory is agent-agnostic and
> dispatches headless Claude, Codex, and Copilot alike."*

And `factory-loop-requirements.md:602` treats host nesting as a **hazard** ("can fan out
inside itself, unmetered and outside the supervisor's model"), never a capability.

**Two measurements undercut the premise rather than the principle.** First, the
agnosticism is hollow in practice: of 338 run records, `claude` 156 and `manual` 182 —
**codex and copilot have zero dispatches, ever**, while the README advertises all three.
Second, D6's decisive row — light mode has *"one window shared by everything"*, therefore
*"light cannot replace dark"* (`factory-loop-requirements.md:629,634`) — is contradicted by
this repo's own measurement at `steering-surfaces-design.md:25`, which records a subagent
body as *"never enters the parent … low — isolated context"*. **Subagents are isolated, not
shared.** The stated reason for refusing host-native dispatch does not hold.

## What must survive any replacement

Not everything in D6 is refuted, and these are the non-negotiables:

- **D1's singleton deterministic supervisor** owning the base checkout and the serial merge
  queue (`factory-design.md:47-61`). A host fan-out must not become a second writer.
- **D9's prompt-hash reproducibility** — *"two runs of the same node are diffable"*
  (`factory-design.md:295`). `prompt_sha256` is already recorded and must stay meaningful.
- **Metering.** The hazard `flr:602` names is real: a host-spawned agent that fans out
  inside itself is invisible to `run-records.json`. Whatever replaces `-p` must record
  spend per unit of work or the spend ceiling (5 correct firings) stops working.
- **Agent-agnosticism as a contract**, even if unexercised: the host path must be one
  runner among several, not a hard dependency on Claude.

## Open question this bead must answer before it builds

Whether the host runtime can be driven **non-interactively from the engine** at all, or
only from a live session — because the supervisor is a subprocess, not a session. If only
the latter, this becomes "the engine emits work the session executes", which is a
different design and should be re-scoped rather than forced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a unit of work, when it is dispatched through the host runtime, then its spend is
  recorded in `run-records.json` exactly as a `-p` dispatch is - check: a test asserts a
  record with non-zero tokens and a `prompt_sha256` exists after a host dispatch.
- Given concurrent host dispatches, when they land, then the serial merge queue and the
  singleton supervisor lock still hold - check: a test asserts two host lanes cannot both
  write the base checkout.
- Given a repo whose configured runner is not claude, when a dispatch is requested, then
  the engine still dispatches - check: a test asserts the host path is one runner among
  several and does not become mandatory.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner host` completes a unit of work without spawning
`claude -p`, and `uv run basicly usage` shows its spend.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `150000`
- depends on: none

for `--agents`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--mcp-config`, `--permission-mode`, `--resume`.

And the agents we do project are inert: `.claude/agents/` holds three files written by
`agents.sync()`, and **no dispatch code reads that directory** — its only other consumer
is `cli.py:1261`, which globs it to *delete* files.

## The decision this contradicts, stated so it is not overturned by accident

`agent-roster-design.md:210` refuses this by name:

> role prompts *"cannot be Claude subagent files — the factory is agent-agnostic and
> dispatches headless Claude, Codex, and Copilot alike."*

And `factory-loop-requirements.md:602` treats host nesting as a **hazard** ("can fan out
inside itself, unmetered and outside the supervisor's model"), never a capability.

**Two measurements undercut the premise rather than the principle.** First, the
agnosticism is hollow in practice: of 338 run records, `claude` 156 and `manual` 182 —
**codex and copilot have zero dispatches, ever**, while the README advertises all three.
Second, D6's decisive row — light mode has *"one window shared by everything"*, therefore
*"light cannot replace dark"* (`factory-loop-requirements.md:629,634`) — is contradicted by
this repo's own measurement at `steering-surfaces-design.md:25`, which records a subagent
body as *"never enters the parent … low — isolated context"*. **Subagents are isolated, not
shared.** The stated reason for refusing host-native dispatch does not hold.

## What must survive any replacement

Not everything in D6 is refuted, and these are the non-negotiables:

- **D1's singleton deterministic supervisor** owning the base checkout and the serial merge
  queue (`factory-design.md:47-61`). A host fan-out must not become a second writer.
- **D9's prompt-hash reproducibility** — *"two runs of the same node are diffable"*
  (`factory-design.md:295`). `prompt_sha256` is already recorded and must stay meaningful.
- **Metering.** The hazard `flr:602` names is real: a host-spawned agent that fans out
  inside itself is invisible to `run-records.json`. Whatever replaces `-p` must record
  spend per unit of work or the spend ceiling (5 correct firings) stops working.
- **Agent-agnosticism as a contract**, even if unexercised: the host path must be one
  runner among several, not a hard dependency on Claude.

## Open question this bead must answer before it builds

Whether the host runtime can be driven **non-interactively from the engine** at all, or
only from a live session — because the supervisor is a subprocess, not a session. If only
the latter, this becomes "the engine emits work the session executes", which is a
different design and should be re-scoped rather than forced.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner host` completes a unit of work without spawning
`claude -p`, and `uv run basicly usage` shows its spend.

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`$?` after `cmd | tail` is `tail`'s status, so a failing gate reports success. The repo already carries
this as prose guidance and it keeps happening: **twice in one session on 2026-08-20**, once reading a
validate exit code and once reading `basicly board validate`, and previously as a background run that
notified "exit code 0" while the gate had failed.

Why it recurs is measurable rather than a matter of care. Per `basicly usage report` on 2026-08-20,
`head` is the **most used** terminal tool in this repository at 16394 invocations and `tail` is **third**
at 13960. The trap sits on the single most travelled path an agent takes, and the guidance against it is
a sentence in a fragment competing with everything else in the always on budget.

Prose has been tried. What has not been tried is a mechanical check. The proposal, for owner decision
because it changes a hook surface: a `PreToolUse` or `PostToolUse` hook that flags a shell command
whose pipeline ends in `head`, `tail` or `grep` **and** whose output the caller then treats as a
pass or fail signal - or, far simpler and cheaper, guidance that a gate is run with its output
redirected to a file and the summary line read from it, which removes the pipe rather than policing it.

**Do not weaken this to a note that says be careful.** The failure mode of the current control is
precisely that it is a note.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any failing command piped into tail, for example `uv run pytest -q tests/some_failing.py | tail -3`.
2. Read `$?`.
3. Observe it is 0 while the command failed.
4. Run the same command without the pipe and observe a non zero status, which is the positive control.
5. Search the always on guidance and observe the rule is present as prose, so the recurrence is not caused by its absence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a shell pipeline whose exit status is read when the guidance or a hook is applied then the operator is directed to PIPESTATUS or to a redirected file rather than the pipe's own status - check: `uv run basicly hooks-check`
- Given the control is a hook then it does not fire on a pipeline whose status is never read, so it refuses the defect and not the idiom

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`

## Working Set

- `.basicly/core/`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly hooks-check`

## Trigger

When I make a cost claim or defend one of our numbers against a vendor's, I want the always-on baseline to already refuse the two moves that went wrong on 2026-09-13, so I can stop re-deriving a conclusion the owner has to overturn with a measurement.

## Requirements

R1. A reader of the baseline is refused the argument before making it, not corrected after.
R2. The two clauses sit with the evidence rules they extend, so a reader meets them in one place.
R3. The addition does not push any always-on file past its gate, and the declared token cost matches what it actually costs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the `external-facts` fragment is rebuilt, then it carries a clause stating that a cost claim names its priced components and never a token count. [check: `uv run basicly catalog lint`]
- When the `external-facts` fragment is rebuilt, then its two-derivation bullet carries a clause stating that a disagreement reported by a person against a third party's own figure is settled by running the third party's path, not by defending ours. [check: `uv run basicly catalog lint`]
- When `always-on-size` runs after the rebuild, then every target is inside its limit. [check: `uv run python .scripts/check_always_on_size.py`]
- When `catalog lint` runs, then the fragment's declared `token_cost` for all three targets is within tolerance of the measured cost. [check: `uv run basicly catalog lint`]
- When the projection gates run, then no generated file is stale. [check: `uv run basicly check` and `uv run basicly skills-check`]

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly catalog lint` then `uv run python .scripts/check_always_on_size.py`

## The two proposals, and the incidents behind them

**One. A cost claim names its priced components, never a token count.** On 2026-09-13 I argued over three turns that a long-lived warm agent session costs more than a fresh one, from token totals. A measurement of five live dispatches reversed it: the totals agreed to within 4% and the cost differed by 5x, because the cache write fell from about 21,000 tokens to about 550 and a write and a read are not the same price. The owner had said the design was right and I kept arguing. Evidence: basicly-8724lqq.

**Two. A disagreement a person reports against a third party's own figure is settled by running the third party's path.** The owner said our recorded costs did not match what the vendor's own interface showed. The fragment already says to treat a two-path disagreement as an instrument fault first, and I defended our number instead of running the vendor's path. When I finally ran it, the answer was that our figures are the vendor's own `result` object read verbatim and the dollar amounts carry `costBasis: list`, so they are a list-price equivalent rather than anything a subscription paid. The rule existed; what was missing is that it also binds when the second path is the owner's report rather than a second derivation of ours. Evidence: basicly-zk24ktw.

## Why one record and not two

Both clauses edit `.basicly/core/fragments/decisions/external-facts.fragment.yaml`. Two records would put two lanes on one file and the scope gate would refuse the second. One record, two criteria.

## Sizing

Measured 2026-09-13, `uv run python .scripts/check_always_on_size.py`: CLAUDE.md 8,801 of 12,000 characters, AGENTS.md 16,126 of 24,576 bytes, copilot-instructions.md 8,900 of 12,000 characters. The fragment declares 188 tokens for claude and codex and 187 for copilot. Two clauses on an existing fragment cost far less than a new fragment, which is why this extends rather than adds - a scoped fragment costs roughly 1,500 characters of the AGENTS.md budget, and the retention measurement shows the tail of an always-on file is what a session loses first.

payload.text:
AMENDED 2026-09-16 after a second session on the same fragment. A third clause is added and the record still edits one file, so it stays one lane.

**THE NEW CLAUSE: a probe that returns something bounds what it proves, and a confound is named before the result is reported.** The fragment already carries the mirror - an empty probe is not evidence of absence. Today produced three instances of the positive form going wrong:

- One fallback defect was found in `claude_stream_usage` and reported as "the instrument is broken". A positive control then showed the fallback reached **2 of 294** records and the recorded history was the vendor's own figures read verbatim.
- One grep of `src/basicly/*.py` returned nothing for the kits, reported as "the kits do not come with basicly install". They ship through the catalog, force-included into the engine wheel at `basicly/catalog`, which a second probe measured at 39 files across all three kits.
- Two Copilot agents loaded and ran, reported as settling whether that host honours a declared tier. Both declared `tier: high`, which resolves to `claude-opus-5`, and the configured default is **also** `claude-opus-5`. The two hypotheses predicted the same observation, so the run decided nothing. The confound was found only by reading `assistant_usage_events` afterwards.

The third is the one a rule catches. **Where two hypotheses predict the same observation, say so before reporting, and change the probe until they differ** - here, by choosing a tier whose model differs from the default.

So the record now carries three changes to `external-facts`, not two: the cost-components clause, the owner-reported-disagreement clause on the existing two-derivation bullet, and this one.

payload.description:
## Context

`retrospector` is authored, projected to both agent roots, vendored to consumers, loads the `root-cause` skill, and has a `ROLE_BY_PHASE` entry (`roles.py:69`, `retrospective -> retrospector`). It can never be invoked, because RETROSPECTIVE is not a phase: `loop._HANDLERS` has seven keys and `retrospective` is not among them, and `config.LOOP_PHASES` does not carry it.

So the harness ships a role, a skill and a map entry for a state that does not exist. That is a dead definition of the same shape the catalog eval exists to catch, one layer up.

## Why this is the mechanism half of the architectural work, not a loop nicety

`factory-loop.md` section 3.2 is explicit that RETROSPECTIVE is **not a lane state**: it is a conditional process over the gate-failure ledger, fired by a *computed* signal.

- Special cause - a point beyond three sigma, or a non-random run or trend inside the limits - fires it.
- Common cause - a single failure inside the limits - **does not**. Acting on that is tampering, which Deming's funnel experiment shows *increases* variation in a stable process.

That guard is the thing the architectural work actually needs. Without it every smell is worth a bead, which is how a backlog of thirteen findings accumulates and never drains. With it, the system answers *is this shape worth acting on* deterministically, from its own ledger, before any judged dispatch is paid for.

This repo has the anti-pattern on record: beads were filed off single occurrences during the very session that produced the requirements document, and `basicly-jr0l` carries twelve follow-ups that named one truncation while none asked why the trigger fired.

## What must be built

1. The state, with an entry predicate that is the computed signal rather than a phase transition - so it is not a rung in the lane ladder and a lane never sits in it.
2. The signal itself, over the recorded gate-failure history: a point beyond three sigma, or a non-random run or trend within the limits.
3. The dispatch of `retrospector` when it fires, metered like every other dispatch.
4. The output contract already specified in section 3.2: a named control, its tier (control / warning / documentation), and the class of defects it covers - never the why-chain. A documentation-tier outcome is recorded as a downgrade with the reason no stronger control was available.
5. Under D25, the output lands as a **diff against catalog YAML**, never as prose advice, and never reaches the catalog without a human at any grant level.

## Acceptance

- Given a gate-failure history with no special-cause signal, when the ledger is evaluated, then RETROSPECTIVE does not fire and no dispatch is made.
- Given a recorded point beyond three sigma, when the ledger is evaluated, then RETROSPECTIVE fires and names the point that triggered it.
- Given a non-random run or trend inside the control limits, when the ledger is evaluated, then RETROSPECTIVE fires and names which of the two patterns it detected.
- Given RETROSPECTIVE fires, when the engine resolves the role, then `roles.resolve_role` returns `retrospector` and it reaches the dispatch argv.
- Given a completed retrospective, when its output is read, then it carries a named control, a tier from control/warning/documentation, and the defect class it covers, and it is expressed as a diff against a catalog source rather than as prose.
- Given the same output, when it is applied, then a human approves it regardless of the autonomy level in force.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop status <issue>` reports the retrospective signal and its inputs, and a seeded ledger with a three-sigma point drives one dispatch end to end.
payload.title: make retrospective a state fired by a special cause signal

## Context

Tier 2 of basicly-ze8z: semi-deterministic, so a script for the facts plus a skill for the judgment.

The runbook for driving a supervised run does not exist in the catalog. Measured: `loop supervise` appears only in `docs/design/factory-design.md` and `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, which describe the system rather than how to drive it, and in the `harness-client` skill, which is about attaching as a second observer. payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-07-31 during the `basicly-5ltn` lane, incidental to that change and not caused by it.
`tests/test_hooks.py::test_sync_hooks_prunes_hook_excluded_by_selection` failed once under
`pytest -q -n 4`, then passed on re-run and in the final full run.

Reported cause: a `shutil.copytree` over the catalog hooks directory raced a **vanishing**
`__pycache__/*.pyc.<tmp>` file. CPython writes a bytecode cache as a uniquely named temp file and then
renames it, so a concurrent tree walk can stat a name that no longer exists by the time it is opened.
With `-n 4` several workers import the same hook scripts at once, so the window is real rather than
theoretical.

This is the same family as `basicly-m4zv.14` (a machine-global beads write lock making gates flaky) -
a flake in a gate costs more than its own runtime, because it burns the loop's bounded rework budget
and trains an operator to re-run rather than read. It is P3 because it is rare and self-clearing, not
because it is harmless.

Two candidate fixes worth weighing rather than assuming:

- Copy with an ignore predicate that skips `__pycache__` entirely (`shutil.ignore_patterns`), which is
  also strictly correct - a bytecode cache is never catalog content and should not be projected or
  compared.
- Run the affected tests with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, which removes the writer rather than
  tolerating it. Note the `basicly-kjc5.61` lane independently hit a *different* `__pycache__` defect
  the same day - a mutation and its restore had identical size and same-second mtime, so a stale `.pyc`
  was reused and silently polluted the next mutation result - and fixed it exactly this way. So the
  same environment variable resolves two separate incidents, which argues for it.

Prefer the fix that also makes `check_hooks` and `sync_hooks` ignore `__pycache__` on principle: the
directory is machine-local build output, so including it in a catalog comparison can only ever produce
false drift.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `uv run pytest -q -n 4` repeatedly on a tree whose `.basicly/core/hooks/__pycache__` is being
  written by concurrent imports.
- Observed, intermittently: `test_sync_hooks_prunes_hook_excluded_by_selection` fails inside
  `shutil.copytree` on a `.pyc.<tmp>` path that no longer exists. Expected: the test is independent of
  bytecode cache files and cannot see them at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given concurrent bytecode cache writes under the catalog hooks directory when the hook sync and
  hook check paths run then no bytecode cache file is copied compared or reported as drift and the
  affected test passes deterministically under parallel pytest, with tests
payload.title: Stop a pycache race making the hook sync test flake under parallel pytest

## Steps to Reproduce

`.basicly/core/fragments/tools/non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml:15` is an always-on bullet on
every surface and reads:

> Use non-interactive flags (`cp -f`, `mv -f`, `rm -f`, package-manager `-y`, ...) for ops that
> can hang on a prompt

For the common case - removing a scratch **directory** - following that literally produces
`rm -rf <dir>`, and `.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml` denies every spelling of it
(`rm -rf*`, `rm -fr*`, `rm -r -f*`, `rm -f -r*`). The agent is steered by the always-on guidance
straight into a hard-denied command.

Observed 2026-07-31 during the v0.6.0 session: a scratch-dir reset was denied mid-task and cost a
turn to rewrite. It is a repeat - the same collision is already recorded in the operator's own
notes from an earlier session, so the guidance has now mis-steered at least twice.

Expected: the fragment names the recursive case and the allowed spelling, so the always-on text
and the deny-list agree.

Proposed fix (do not self-apply - this is a retro finding): extend the bullet to say that a
recursive delete uses `rm -r` and that the force variants are denied, e.g. "... for ops that can
hang on a prompt - but a recursive delete is `rm -r`, never `rm -rf`, which the deny-list blocks
outright; prefer a uniquely named fresh directory over clearing an old one." Cost is a few dozen
chars on all three surfaces; headroom at the time of filing was CLAUDE.md ~1060,
copilot-instructions ~926, AGENTS.md ~1167, so it fits - confirm before landing.

payload.description:
When a release refuses because the tutorial names the old version, I want the reason written down, so I can stop someone adding docs/tutorial to the pin globs and quietly falsifying a transcript.

docs/tutorial/first-loop.md opens by claiming every command and every quoted output was executed in a real terminal on a named version. docs-claims enforces that the named version is the newest released one, so a release refuses until the page is re-recorded. That refusal is the gate working.

Adding docs/tutorial to release.PIN_GLOBS looks like the obvious fix and is the wrong one. The pin pattern matches the @vX.Y.Z install line, which is a command, but the page also carries engine: basicly X.Y.Z inside recorded output. Rewriting those would make the opening sentence false while the gate went green. I made that change during v0.14.0 and reverted it.
payload.requirements: no gate is weakened and no waiver is added: the release stays refused until a human re-records the page
payload.title: record why the tutorial is not a release pin target

payload.text:
Re-recorded for v0.14.0 on 2026-09-18. A fresh git repository, basicly installed from a locally built 0.14.0 wheel, then every step of the page walked: install, status, gitignore, policy scaffold, tracker create, policy dor, the install commit, loop status, loop run to the classify checkpoint, the worktree edit and its commit, the landing, the ship approval, git log and the closing loop status.

Every quoted block matched what the page already said apart from ids, commit hashes and sub-second timings. basicly status was identical field for field. The six commits came out in the same shapes and the same order. So the five version strings were the only edit the page needed, and the opening sentence is true.

Two things the recording had to route around, neither a page defect. The shell is not a TTY, so a checkpoint prints a one-time code rather than taking the terminal as the human - which the page already documents as the relay. And loop run --confirm refuses the ship checkpoint whatever code it is given, because the advance reissues the code before reading it; policy checkpoint <id> ship --approve --confirm is the surface that works. The page never shows either, because a reader at a terminal meets neither.

A structural fact that decides how this can ever be done: basicly release tags locally and deliberately does not push, so @vX.Y.Z is unreachable until after the release. The page can only be recorded against a locally built engine, with the git+ line as the documented equivalent.

payload.title: the two board producer modules land at eighteen and twenty three tokens so no further board unit fits

payload.text:
Closed by a4137c04. lint-imports 2 kept 0 broken; full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4475 tests.

Two modules became four, and the split line is the one this record named.

  board_fields    1809 -> 1607   headroom 18 -> 2393   bounds, and a marker as fields
  board_sections     new 2846    headroom      1154    the six row reducers, and LaneFacts
  board_snapshot  2280 -> 2845   headroom 23 -> 1155   the ledger half, and build_document
  board_usage        new 1324    headroom      2676    the .basicly/usage/ sections

Neither seam imports back. Both new modules got their own tier under the exhaustive contract, so a maintainer decided placement rather than the gate inferring it. The architecture layering block is regenerated, not edited, as the third criterion required: 39 tiers to 41, 105 modules to 107.

The third acceptance criterion is REFUTED, with the measurement. It asked for no new density waiver. Splitting raises the prose share of both halves by construction - the code divides, the contract docstring does not. board_snapshot lost 630 tokens of code and 505 of prose in one edit: 3980 to 2845 tokens and 47 to 51.5 percent, smaller and denser at once. Every cheaper reduction was taken first and measured at each step, 55.7 and 55.1 down to 51.5 both: prose moved to the module whose code it describes, two stale cross-references THE SPLIT ITSELF created were repointed, two restatements of test assertions dropped. What is left is measurements plus a ruff D mandated Args block that is a third of board_snapshot's prose. No rebalancing avoids the waivers: folding board_usage back gives 4169 against the 4000 cap, and extracting the three facts records instead gives a module that is 89 percent prose. Two stated waivers, count_delta = 2, reasoning in basicly.d/basicly-y754k2.toml.

Three defects my own refactoring introduced, each caught before it landed. A @dataclass decorator was separated from its class by my block partitioner - caught by an assertion I put in the script. A regex qualification rewrote the dictionary KEY string 'text' into 'board_fields.text' - caught by ruff E501, then redone token-aware, 50 rewrites and 0 string-literal damage. A rename turned a definition line into 'board_usage.DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER_S = 60.0', an assignment into another module - caught by reading the grep rather than trusting it. payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 3. basicly drift means config drift only. Derive a per-repo/per-agent health signal from the run-record log and flag behavioral regressions against a rolling baseline.

Design note (found while scoping): br gate results have no history — they overwrite in br (policy.py), so gate pass/fail over time is not queryable. The durable historical signal is the run-record log (.basicly/usage/run-records.json): append-only, keyed by bead, carrying agent + outcome (executed/failed/handoff) + timestamp. A failed dispatch is a failed run and a rework re-dispatch appends another record for the same bead, so run-record outcomes are a durable proxy for the gate-fail + rework signal without coupling to br's non-historical gate state. Signal source decided with the user: run-records only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New src/basicly/health.py (sibling to fleet.py, imports run_record only) with pure functions: agent_health(records_by_bead) and agent_drift(records_by_bead, window) plus health_report(repo_root, window). No new br calls and no new persisted state.
- Per-agent health covers: runs, counts by outcome, failure_rate (failed / dispatched runs, handoffs excluded), a rework signal (count of beads that agent re-dispatched), and a documented bounded health_score in [0,1] computed from named weight constants at module top.
- Rolling-baseline drift: an agent's most-recent window runs (recent window) are compared against all older runs (baseline window), sorted by the record timestamp. A behavioral regression is flagged when the recent failure_rate exceeds the baseline failure_rate by a documented regression delta AND both windows meet a documented minimum sample size, so a couple of runs cannot trip it.
- basicly health [--json] [--window N] prints a per-agent summary plus any flagged regressions for the current repo; --fleet [--root PATH] rolls up per-repo health via fleet.discover_repos. Read-only, always exits 0; a repo or agent with no run-records degrades to an empty report, not an error.
- Schema-versioned JSON payload like status/fleet; no wall-clock value in the payload so output is deterministic.
- Regression tests mirror tests/test_fleet.py and the run-record fixtures: the health math, drift regression / no-regression / insufficient-sample, empty and corrupt log resilience, CLI dispatch, and a docs-drift entry for the new command.
- docs/architecture.md dimension-3 (observability) updated to describe the health/drift signal and why gate-history is not a source; pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

Signal is run-records only (decided with the user): no live br gate/rework querying, so it works on the durable log alone and stays deterministic. No token/cost health (those run-record fields are still null, reserved). No time-series storage or charting — drift is computed from the existing log's timestamps, not a new persisted baseline file. health_score weights and drift thresholds are documented module constants, advisory only (nothing gates on them). The --fleet roll-up reuses fleet.discover_repos; it does not replace the existing status --fleet run-record summary.

## Trigger
Verifying the v0.13.0 release page after publishing, 2026-09-12.

## Defect
Two sites in the v0.13.0 section said `init` writes the kit skill into `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` and `.github/skills/`. The same section, twelve lines later and again at the fixed entry, says the third copy was removed. The release notes contradicted themselves, and the contradiction was published.

`changelog.d/basicly-witw3qh.added.md` was written when the installer did write three roots. `basicly-hzkl3am` changed the behaviour two commits before the release and corrected the kit READMEs, the installer and the tests - but not the changelog fragment already sitting in `changelog.d/` describing the old behaviour. I also appended the fix sentence to the summary paragraph without editing the claim above it.

## Why no gate caught it
`release-fragments` checks that a fragment exists and fits 400 characters. `docs-claims` checks commands and generated blocks. Nothing reads a fragment against the code it describes, and nothing notices two statements in one section disagreeing.

## Fix applied
Both sites corrected in CHANGELOG.md and the published release body updated.

## Worth considering, not filed as work
A fragment is written when the work lands and read at release time, so any later change in the same cycle can invalidate it. The cheap check is a release-time prompt listing fragments whose scope paths were touched by a later commit.

- `CHANGELOG.md`
